title: War and Peace
subtitle: For whom does the bell toll?

trails.title: Heavy Door
trails.description: No invitation, no key, no requirements. Just give it a knock.

content.text:
Five days have passed since the Mărțișor.

Grandma Jina received several amulets and gave them to Elena and me. Grandma Jina said that this amulet was for saying goodbye to winter and welcoming spring, but I saw some yellow powder mixed into the white hemp thread, I thought it might be daffodil powder, but Elena told me not to think too much—it couldn't have come from the cemetery.

Elena tied a knot on my amulet just like hers, so everyone would know we're sisters. She was so excited for Grandma Jina to see her handiwork that she didn't even take the time to read to me today—she just kept dragging me in front of Grandma Jina, but even now, as I write in my diary, Grandma Jina still hasn't said anything, and Elena has fallen asleep. Maybe she'll forget it tomorrow, but I'll remember it for a long time, because I want to tell her that we can't be sisters. The children in the orphanage don't have relatives. But I never said that.

There are exceptions, though, like if Elena and I are taken away by the same person, or the same couple, then we'll become sisters by law ...

The door of the orphanage is a very heavy door. I don't know how my parents managed to open it and send me inside, but maybe there are a lot of adults who can't open that door like me, so they couldn't come back to get their children. If someone knocks on the door and wants to come in, I'll run over to help them, and then I'll ask them to take me and Elena with them, and if possible, Andre as well ...

But it's okay if no one comes to knock on the door, because the three of us are together now.

items.text: War and Peace

I looked at it, the ring of life, the ring of all lives.
                    Your hands form the ring, and the judgment is pronounced.
                    On the doomsday, at the dusk when history fades away.
                    Oh world! Its head bites its feet, its knees touch its nose.
                    Oh man! They inhabit the earth, waiting for the sky to fall.
                    Yesterday turns into tomorrow, tomorrow reverts to yesterday.
                    Who shall vanish in the rain?

Who shall be granted the eternal happiness, the grace from above—
                    And that emptiness, the cessation of existence?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What is it that you want, Isolde?!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I thought the Foundation was exaggerating the truth. But you, you are ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Are you mad, doctor? Because I killed Mr. Karl?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... I thought it would make you happy.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Happy? Why would I be happy?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Because he was a boastful man, his ideas were at odds with yours, and he contributed to the repression of this era. A bureaucrat you hate the most.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He treated us like stains on the wall to be covered up in shame. And he was the kind of man who'd pocket the gold foil whenever he found any.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Society is dying because of these hypocrites. Don't you think we should have the surgery and remove them?
Her words, mad as they are, manage to convey a warm sincerity.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... I didn't know ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I didn't know you would interpret my words this way.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I deeply regret ever telling you that ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... What?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Why? Why are you being so cruel to me?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It was you who said that everyone was sick and dying, even though they pretended to be fine.  Yet the source of the sickness lay not in ourselves, but in the twisted era we lived in.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: A radical surgery is the only way to remove this ugly tumor ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And it was also you who told me to stop repressing and to embrace my desires. We should restore the world to what it was like, a kingdom of freedom where everyone will be happy ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Are these not your words? Or have I misunderstood them?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Why won't you look at me? Have I made such a big mistake that you don't want to see me again?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: No, no, no ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Please answer me, I'm begging you. You are my only friend and the one I cherish most in the whole world ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor, what on earth have I done wrong? Why won't you forgive me?
Kakania's stone-like visage does not crack.
Isolde chokes dramatically.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Is it because ... I'm too stupid to understand your words?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Or because I'm also sick with the incurable tumor?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: If that's the case, please help me ... Hold my hands, touch my face, hug me, and talk to me heart to heart like you used to.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor, doctor ...
Isolde approaches.
She reaches out a grasping hand at a fleeting corner of her garment.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... I saw myself in that dream of yours, like looking into a mirror.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It was dusk when we had that conversation. It was the first time in my life that I saw the sun.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Your dream filled my empty life with meaning. You saved me from being just a cursed vessel.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: That was a beautiful dream ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: So beautiful that I forgot how ugly I was while staring at it.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I'm just trying to realize your dream.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Am I ... wrong?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... I never thought you would commit a crime over my words.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Crime? You mean what I'm doing right now? You don't like it?
She steps forward anxiously, fearing she might miss something.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The Foundation knows all the truths, yet they won't tell us anything.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: That's why we have to release everything they repress ... the news, the hysteria, the riots, the chaos. That's what Manus Vindictae told me.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Is this not like your dream? Did I misunderstand?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What? What in the world did they tell you?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Heh heh ... They told me the method of salvation, doctor.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: They gave me the opportunity to save your loved ones, the world, and your dream.
The fall is painful.
The space below the stage feels unexpectedly vast.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: *coughs*

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Where am I?
Backstage, Vienna People's Opera
Enormous props fill the back area, with black and white shadows painted directly onto the floor.
Forming another stage beneath the stage.
A familiar scent lingers in the air, prompting Marcus to rub her nose.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: *coughs* I've smelled this before ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Welcome, Angelotti, and Unknown Lady from the Foundation.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Welcome to the small beginning of our new world.
On the stage, he still gives a perfect impression of a harmless gentleman.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text:
Whoa! Sleeping bullets from Laplace ... You almost hit me, miss!
I can't let you through, though, not now. The leading actress is busy.
Heinrich complains, hopping to the side and out of the bullet's path.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The curtain has been raised, ladies, and the show is about to begin. Why not open your hearts before the lights come on?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Let's sit down and have a civilized conversa—whoa!
This next bullet fires true, but the air is so clouded with dust that the target had already moved before it struck.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: There is no need to negotiate with a terrorist.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: You will have the chance to talk to our specialist after I take you to the headquarters.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: A terrorist? You wound me!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Is it because I wear the mask of Manus? Because I revealed the truth you've been hiding? Or because ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: ... we accelerated the "Storm" and made this era end earlier than expected?
A  glow of arcane skill breaks through in response to his query.
Marcus raises her hand, the lamp dispelling some of the darkness.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Let me help you, Madam Hofmann!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: My Angelotti, why are you standing with the enemy? You're supposed to be one of us.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Angelotti ...? Is that me?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: I am your "salvation," from the real terrorists of the world!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... "Salvation"?
This familiar term catches her ears, burning in them.
This ordinary word has become most irritating.
The speech, given from the cover of the props, continues.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Angelotti with a full case of books! Tell me, of all the books you have read and all the documents you have worked with, did any of them ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: ... mention the catastrophe that suddenly broke out in the summer of 1914?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The scourge of the 20th century, the real history!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You have such a kind heart, doctor, yet you don't know the truth. How are you going to bear the pain when you do?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Theophil set himself on fire, Ben hanged himself to death, Emmanuel laid himself on the railroad tracks ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Are they the suicide cases in Vienna? They all came into contact with the Manus?
Isolde tilts her head back, laughing brokenly.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Heh heh, hahahaha ... I can see them, I can hear them, the ghosts of future history, haunting the city from above!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Heads full of holes! Heads covered in shrapnel! Empty stomachs! Even the ghosts of little children ... I can see them all! Cities bombed to the ground, and trains full of people headed straight for death!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It is coming, IT IS COMING! By then, the guts hanging from trees will be more vibrant than spring flowers! There will be bullets, helmets, gauze! Hahaha!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: We have no future, doctor!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: How I wish it were a farce, a farce that claimed the lives of more than ten million people, a farce that dozens of leaders decided to take part in.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: ... Ben, a dear friend of mine ... He played the best Fantasia in A Minor ever, but came back from the battlefield missing an arm and a leg.
He remembers that day. When the generous Mr. Forget Me Not stepped across the deck, his questions stifled by a stack of thick letters.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: And Emmanuel. His hands were born to write poetry, but he was sent to the front and dug trenches until he died of disease.
When did Emanuel stop painting? He could not even recall his old friend's handwriting ... It was blurry now.
Only his anger remains vivid.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Our hands are meant to hold paintbrushes, play pianos, and write stories ... but they end up in gunfire because you narrow-minded hypocrites keep inciting them to violence.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: We've already suffered for our gifts. Now we have to watch our talented friends sacrifice themselves for man's childish tantrums.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Ladies, you know all of this ... yet you call us terrorists?

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: *coughs weakly*
Having been quiet for a worrying amount of time, Hofmann coughs up a mouthful of blood, dragging attention back to her.
Hofmann clutches her chest, falling just short of collapsing to her knees.
Her face is now deathly pale, and Marcus watches as the cold face she wears contorts with streaks of pain and unease.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Madam Hofmann? Madam Hofmann!
Heinrich continues to speak, entirely unconcerned.
He points at Hofmann.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: The real terrorists are you, humans!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: It was you who started that war!
TO BE CONTINUED…
